target.title: fix(supervisor): suppress unhandled stream errors on child stdout/stderr
target.body:
## Summary

The core process supervisor (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`) attaches `data`, `end`, and `close` listeners to child process stdout/stderr streams but no `error` handler. If either stream emits an error event (EPIPE from broken pipe, I/O error, resource limit), the unhandled error crashes the Node.js process.

## What Problem This Solves

Every supervised child process (all `supervisor.spawn()` calls) flows through this adapter. A stream-level error on stdout or stderr of any supervised child currently crashes the gateway worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add noop `.on("error", () => {})` handlers on both `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` streams in the `onStdout` and `onStderr` setup functions. This follows the same pattern already used for `child.stdin` in `src/process/exec.ts:613`.

## User Impact

Supervised child process output streams no longer crash the gateway on stream errors. Data/end/close events continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Before**: `child.stdout.on("error")` absent → unhandled stream error → process crash

**After**: `child.stdout.on("error", () => {})` → error suppressed → graceful degradation

**Tests** (18 passed):
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

## Risk

Low. Two one-line additions of noop handlers. Same pattern already used in `src/process/exec.ts:613` for `child.stdin`.
